definitions.gloss: full effort, all one's strength, utmost power
definitions.explanation: Putting everything one has into an action. Used for both physical exertion and mental or emotional commitment.

examples.japanese: {全力|ぜんりょく}で{走|はし}る。
{試験|しけん}に{向|む}けて{全力|ぜんりょく}で{勉強|べんきょう}した。
examples.english: I studied with all my effort for the exam.

examples.japanese: チームの{全員|ぜんいん}が{全力|ぜんりょく}を{尽|つ}くして{戦|たたか}った{結果|けっか}、{優勝|ゆうしょう}できた。
examples.english: As a result of every team member giving their all, we were able to win the championship.

notes:
Often used with で as an adverbial phrase: {全力|ぜんりょく}で (with all one's might).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {全力|ぜんりょく}で{走|はし}る (run at full speed)
- {全力|ぜんりょく}を{尽|つ}くす (give one's all, exhaust one's efforts)
- {全力|ぜんりょく}を{出|だ}す (put out full effort)
- {全力|ぜんりょく}で{取|と}り{組|く}む (tackle something with full effort)
- {全力投球|ぜんりょくとうきゅう} (giving it everything — literally "full-power pitch")

{全力|ぜんりょく}を{尽|つ}くす is a common set phrase meaning to do one's absolute best, often used in speeches and formal encouragement.
